outcome: clinical course of disease during pregnancy and postpartum
cohort: The study included 43 pregnancies with a definitive diagnosis of MS, matched with 100 healthy pregnant women with similar characteristics.
finding: Maternal MS was not associated with adverse maternal and perinatal outcomes, except for increased rates of urinary tract infection, low 1-min Apgar scores, and decreased breastfeeding rates.
mod_finding: Rates of cesarean delivery were comparable between women with and without MS, though general anesthesia during cesarean delivery was more frequent in women with MS.
